name: Borderline Personality (BPD) Test
tagline: Explore emotional intensity, identity and relationship patterns.
intro: This screener looks at five areas linked to borderline personality traits: emotional ups and downs, sense of identity, relationships, impulsive behaviour and fear of abandonment. Answer based on how often each statement has applied to you over the past year. It takes about five minutes and is not a diagnosis, but it can help you recognise patterns and decide whether to seek professional support.
seoTitle: BPD Test: Free borderline personality screener
seoDescription: Do you experience intense emotions, unstable relationships or fear of abandonment? Take this 5-minute BPD screener and get a personal report.

emotional_instability.name: Emotional intensity
emotional_instability.short: How intense and changeable your emotions are, and how hard they are to calm.
emotional_instability.low: Your answers suggest that your emotions are fairly steady and manageable. You seem to recover from upsets without too much trouble and rarely feel overwhelmed by anger or sadness. That emotional balance is a real strength in stressful times and in relationships. Keep looking after the things that help you stay steady, such as sleep, exercise and people you can talk to.
emotional_instability.mid: Your answers suggest that your emotions sometimes become intense or shift quickly, especially under stress. You may occasionally feel overwhelmed or react more strongly than you would like. Learning to notice early signs, such as tension or racing thoughts, gives you a chance to pause. Simple techniques like slow breathing, a short walk or cold water on your face can help you calm down faster.
emotional_instability.high: Your answers suggest that your emotions are often very intense, change quickly and are hard to calm down. Living with such strong feelings can be exhausting and painful. Emotional intensity like this is a central feature of borderline personality traits, and there are effective therapies, such as DBT, that teach skills to manage it. Please consider talking to a qualified mental health professional. If you are having thoughts of harming yourself, please contact your local emergency services or a crisis line right away.

identity.name: Sense of identity
identity.short: How stable and clear your sense of who you are feels.
identity.low: Your answers suggest that you have a fairly clear and stable sense of who you are and what you value. Your goals and self-image do not seem to shift dramatically depending on circumstances or other people. This inner stability helps you make choices and cope with change. Keep reflecting on your values now and then, as healthy identities still grow over time.
identity.mid: Your answers suggest that your sense of self is sometimes unclear or changeable. You may adapt strongly to the people around you or feel unsure about your direction at times. This is common in periods of change. Writing down what matters to you and noticing which choices feel truly your own can help you build a steadier inner compass over time.
identity.high: Your answers suggest that your sense of who you are often feels unstable, unclear or empty, and that your goals, values and self-image may shift a lot. This can feel confusing and lonely. An unstable sense of identity and chronic emptiness are recognised features of borderline personality traits. Please consider exploring this with a qualified mental health professional, as therapy can help build a steadier sense of self. If you are having thoughts of harming yourself, please contact your local emergency services or a crisis line right away.

relationships.name: Relationships
relationships.short: How intense, stable or turbulent your close relationships tend to be.
relationships.low: Your answers suggest that your close relationships are mostly stable and that you can see both the good and the less good sides of the people around you. Conflicts seem to pass without lasting damage. This balanced view is a solid basis for trust and long-lasting bonds. Keep investing in the people who matter to you, and keep expressing your needs openly so small frustrations do not build up.
relationships.mid: Your answers suggest that your relationships sometimes feel intense or turbulent, with periods of closeness and conflict. You may occasionally swing between strong admiration and disappointment. When you notice an extreme reaction, try to pause and remind yourself of the whole picture of the person. Talking openly about your needs, rather than testing others, often makes relationships calmer and builds more trust over time.
relationships.high: Your answers suggest that your close relationships often feel intense and unstable, swinging between idealising and feeling let down, with frequent conflicts. This pattern can be very painful for you and the people you care about. It is a recognised feature of borderline personality traits, and therapy can help you build calmer, more secure connections. Please consider talking to a qualified mental health professional. If you are having thoughts of harming yourself, please contact your local emergency services or a crisis line right away.

impulsivity.name: Impulsive behaviour
impulsivity.short: How often you act on urges in ways that could harm you, especially when upset.
impulsivity.low: Your answers suggest that you usually keep your behaviour under control, even when emotions run high. You seem to think about consequences before acting and rarely do things you regret. This self-control protects your health, finances and relationships. Keep using the strategies that help you, such as pausing or talking things through before you act. Stress and tiredness can weaken anyone's self-control, so plan extra care during demanding periods.
impulsivity.mid: Your answers suggest that you sometimes act on impulse when you are upset, for example by spending, eating, drinking or saying things you regret. Many people use quick fixes to cope with strong emotions. Try to identify your typical triggers and plan a healthier alternative in advance, such as calling a friend, going for a walk or waiting twenty minutes before acting.
impulsivity.high: Your answers suggest that you often act on urges that could harm you, especially when emotions run high, for example with money, substances, food, driving or relationships. These behaviours are often attempts to cope with overwhelming feelings. Please consider talking to a qualified mental health professional who can help you find safer ways to cope. If you are having thoughts of harming yourself, please contact your local emergency services or a crisis line right away. Reducing easy access to things you use impulsively can also help.

abandonment.name: Fear of abandonment
abandonment.short: How strongly you fear being left, rejected or alone.
abandonment.low: Your answers suggest that you generally feel secure in your relationships and are not overly worried about being left. You can give others space and cope with time alone. This sense of security makes relationships feel calmer and more trusting. Continue to nurture the connections that make you feel safe and valued. If old worries resurface during a difficult time, talking about them openly usually helps them pass.
abandonment.mid: Your answers suggest that fears of rejection or being left sometimes come up, for example when someone does not reply or seems distant. This is a very human worry, especially after past disappointments. When the fear rises, try to check the facts before acting on it, and soothe yourself with activities you enjoy on your own. Openly sharing your needs can build trust.
abandonment.high: Your answers suggest that a strong fear of being abandoned or rejected often affects how you feel and act in relationships, and that being alone can feel unbearable. This fear can be exhausting and may lead to actions that push people away. It is a recognised feature of borderline personality traits and responds well to therapy. Please consider speaking with a qualified mental health professional. If you are having thoughts of harming yourself, please contact your local emergency services or a crisis line right away.

summary: This screener shows how strongly you recognise five groups of traits associated with borderline personality. Higher scores mean these patterns appear more often in your life. The results are not a diagnosis; only a qualified professional can assess this, and effective help is available. If you are having thoughts of harming yourself, please contact your local emergency services or a crisis line right away.
